name: Growth Projection (Simple)
description: Project a starting value forward across several periods at a constant simple (non-compounding) growth rate.
formula: Projected value = Starting value × (1 + Growth rate × Number of periods)
business_contexts: a company projecting revenue forward at a flat annual growth rate
a retailer projecting store count forward at a steady pace
a city projecting population forward at a steady rate
a nonprofit projecting donor base forward at a flat rate
a utility projecting demand forward at a steady rate
question_patterns: Given the starting value, growth rate, and number of periods below, what is the projected value?
Calculate the projected value after the number of periods shown, at the growth rate given.
What value results from applying the growth rate below across the number of periods shown?
Calculate the projected value using simple (non-compounding) growth applied across the periods given.
Using the figures below, project the starting value forward across the periods shown.
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate total growth factor = growth_rate × periods
Step 2: Calculate projected value = starting_value × (1 + total growth factor)
key_insight: Simple growth applies the rate to the original base every period, unlike compound growth, which applies it to the already-grown value — the two diverge quickly as periods stack up.
common_mistakes: Compounding the rate period over period instead of applying it as simple growth against the original base
Forgetting to multiply the rate by the number of periods before adding it to 1
framework_soundbite: Simple growth is rate times periods, applied once to the starting base — not compounded step by step.
